messages:
mike: Quick follow-up from the quota/abuse RFC — I'm proposing a small "quota signal gateway" between the edge proxies and the central quota bank. goal: isolate edge churn and simplify the bank's admission surface.

anjali: quick sketch? wondering how much extra latency this adds and where caching lives.

mike: sketch: edge -> gateway (per-region, small memory cache + admission heuristics) -> central bank. gateway owns short-lived probes and can return soft-allow with a token id, central bank still authoritative for long-lived reservations.

sara: sounds reasonable. what's the failure model if gateway loses connectivity to bank? do we fail open/closed?

mike: default is fail-soft: gateway can serve previously cached soft-allow for up to X seconds, and then degrade to token-throttling with 429. we want to avoid global load spikes due to transient control plane issues.

lucas: can we enumerate the interfaces? I think a simple gRPC contract: Check(ctx, request) -> {decision, token_id, ttl, score}. then gateway can add its own score tweak.

anjali: +1 on a compact proto. also need a lightweight push from bank -> gateway for priority updates (e.g., tenant eviction).

mike: agreed. bank->gateway push over streaming RPC. gateway also exposes local metrics and tracing breadcrumbs.

jen: curious about fairness: will gateway do per-tenant FIFO or just token buckets? mixing both gets tricky.

sara: my gut: keep gateway simple (token buckets + short probe window). fairness decisions remain central. gateway should not try to enforce complex fairness policies. it can tag requests with local hints for the bank's optimizer.

lucas: what about abuse signals? we already have an abuse pipeline that scores clients every minute. gateway could consume recent abuse scores and apply immediate soft-deny for high-risk clients.

mike: yes, we should allow a modest local blocklist derived from abuse signal feed. important: every local block must be auditable (send event to bank/obs).

anjali: operational questions: how many gateways per region? sticky by edge proxy cluster? we need HA and routing fallback when a gateway is overloaded.

mike: initial plan: 3 replicas per region, sticky hashing from edge cluster id. routing fallback: if gateway returns overloaded, edge falls back to talking directly to the bank (with stricter rate limits).

jen: cost tradeoffs? adding gateways adds CPU and memory and push traffic. but reduces load on bank from short-lived traffic. do we have sim numbers?

lucas: I ran a small sim yesterday: with a 2s local cache TTL for soft-allow we reduce bank qps by ~35% for bursty tenants. CPU per gateway is minimal (mostly networking).

mike: nice. next steps: 1) draft proto (lucas), 2) minimal gateway binary (sara + lucas), 3) integration test with abuse feed + bank failover (anjali). I'll open a tracker.

quota-bot: action created: INFRA-1234 "quota-signal-gateway: proto + PoC" assigned to lucas, sara. due 2w.

anjali: one open concern: how do we version the gateway contract so Dedicated/private customers can opt out? we need backward compatibility flags.

mike: include a header flag 'X-Quota-Gateway-Version' and default to v1. bank will accept v1 and v0 legacy paths. doc it in the proto.

jen: tiny nit: ensure gateway metrics include per-tenant hit/miss so we can judge cache effectiveness.

sara: documented. also will add a debug endpoint to dump decision traces for a request id.

mike: great. if there are no blockers I'll move this to RFC follow-up board and tag eng-sre for HA runbook. low-priority unless we see bank saturation in next 2 sprints.

lucas: ack. I'll start the proto draft later today.

anjali: thanks — will sync on Thursday to review the PoC results.

mike: thanks all :thumbsup:
